html:
The Tapachultec were the people of the area around Tapachula, on the Pacific coast of Chiapas near the border with Guatemala. They spoke a Mixe-Zoquean language, related to Mixe and Zoque, which died out in the 1900s.

Their region, the Soconusco, was one of the richest cacao lands of Mesoamerica, and around 1500 it was conquered by the Aztec Triple Alliance, which took its cacao as tribute. Long before, the same coast was home to some of the earliest pottery-making villages of Mesoamerica. Little else is recorded about the Tapachultec as a people.
